correctness.rationale: Arbitrary antiderivative tests in x, y, and z give the three conditional expectations. Each conditional residual is exactly one coordinate speed up to the displayed coefficient, so L2 orthogonality gives all three variance and covariance identities. If any speed defect vanishes, the corresponding coordinate is constant on every bounded complete support trajectory; stable-filter or scalar-product reductions then force the trajectory into the real equilibrium set. Conversely all equilibrium-supported invariant measures have zero speed defects. The packaged checker independently verifies the residual algebra, regression decompositions, and classical equilibrium equations.

originality.rationale: The strongest same-family published comparison is a stationary-balance theorem for the complex Chen extension. On the real subspace it yields integrated first- and second-moment identities but not conditional disintegrations. A complete same-object bifurcation treatment covers symmetry, stability, dissipativity, equilibria, periodic bifurcations, coexistence, and attractor geometry without a matching conditional-moment theorem. The accepted statement is strictly stronger than the prior integrated relations because each conditional equality represents an infinite family of test-function orthogonality constraints.

The 2024 complex-Chen publisher page exposed the abstract, classification, references, and figures but not the paywalled full article body.
The generator argument is short enough that an equivalent fiberwise identity may occur under different terminology in unindexed literature.

No novelty is claimed for the Chen equations, equilibria, symmetry, dissipativity, bifurcation structure, attractor geometry, or the integrated real-subspace balances already covered by the published complex-Chen theorem.

value.rationale: The Chen system is a canonical Lorenz-like chaotic flow with well-developed bifurcation and coexistence theory. The accepted theorem assigns exact stationary statistical meaning to all three coordinate couplings, measure by measure, rather than only to one selected numerical attractor or a symmetry-averaged state. The residual speed energies quantify exactly how far each coupling is from perfect predictor-response coherence, while the common equality classification separates equilibrium mixtures from genuinely recurrent motion. These formulas give parameter-exact consistency checks for periodic, chaotic, or mixed invariant states and refine known integrated balances into distributional constraints.
